name: Renogy Rigid Mono 100W
notes: Technology: monocrystalline PERC cells (36-cell at 100 W, 40-cell at 200 W), monofacial, 3.2 mm tempered glass in a black anodised aluminium frame. Pros: a common off-grid and leisure panel with a 12 V-class Vmp that suits small 12/24 V MPPT chargers, and cheap, robust framed construction. Cons: heavy for its output compared with a flexible panel, too low-voltage for a grid-tied string inverter, and the datasheet rates it for 600 V systems only. Notable: the 200 W has a higher Voc (27 V), so two in series on a 100 V charger leaves less cold-weather margin than the 100 W.

name: Renogy Flexible Mono 100W
notes: Technology: 36-cell monocrystalline laminate, monofacial, about 2 mm thick with no glass or frame. Pros: very light (1.9 kg at 100 W, 2.8 kg at 175 W) and bends to fit curved van, boat and caravan roofs, usually bonded on rather than bolted. Cons: lower efficiency than the rigid range, runs hotter when glued flat to a roof (so more heat loss), and flexible laminates generally have a shorter service life than glass panels; rated for 600 V systems.
